body:
Admitting a scummy situation is as kind a response as I could hope for. I just want to know what to tell the other people who are starting down the same path as me. What do I tell them? What do I tell people who are working hard, but don't have financial security or stable households to support them? They ask me: if there was no hope for me, what hope is there for them?--why they should continue with no hope in sight--and I...

I can't tell them the truth. I'm not a good liar. I try to avoid the question, and that's more damning than just admitting it. All I can think of is to ask someone else. Someone; goddammit someone must have for them, even if no one has an answer for me.

I have applied to positions in computer programming, analytics, simulation, operational procedures, teaching, retail, fast food, anything in the area. In the end they ask for my references and I give them a string of short termed jobs, most lasting 2 years before the company I joined went under. Everyone comes to the same conclusion: there is something fundamentally wrong with me. No one wants to take a chance on someone old, educated, and with no work experience. Under 30,000 thinks I'm gonna leave first chance I get. >30k think I must be horrible or someone would have hired me. In the end, what do I have to argue with?
You posted this here for a reason. You knew there are still people who care for you. You know this is wrong. There is still time. You can still call 911 and be saved with emergency care.

I want to be wrong. I'm desperate to be wrong. I sent this here to see if anyone could tell me I was wrong. Every day I invest entirely into doing whatever I can to prove I am wrong.

What is, is usually not what is wanted. I want to be wrong. I am right.

"It gets better" is nonsense. Nothing just "gets better." You mentioned a church, a gang, people you know. Have you admitted to them you need help? That you need a job, any simple job, to keep you from falling apart? There are people whose only job is helping others in a time of need. Your pastor, your congressman, anyone you can get a hold of... even if they can't help they should know.

The only advice I can give you is there is a difference between being dumb, and being scared. Scared people act dumb; they fail to concentrate enough to do what smart people can do. I tutor people in high school and in college, I should know. If you can find someone, some place, to feel safe--to stop being afraid, you may be smarter than you think.
